summary: This is a Java interface: a contract that says any temperature sensor must be able to report a current temperature as a whole number. It contains no code of its own, so real hardware sensors and fake test sensors can both fulfil it in their own way.

lines.text: An interface names a capability rather than a concrete thing, so code that needs a temperature can depend on this name instead of on one particular sensor. Because the type is declared public, Java requires it to live in a file called TemperatureSensor.java.

The method has no body, only a signature ending in a semicolon: every implementing class must supply its own way of producing the reading. That is what makes testing easy, since a test can hand over a stub sensor that always returns 12 instead of waiting for real hardware.
